clue.text: Made out bell? Bet it's some sort of buzzer

indicators.note: made in the sense of fashioned or put together, so the following letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone who has worked out what a bell is wagers that it is a kind of buzzer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' is the anagram signal working on OUT, BELL and BET together; 'it's' links them to the definition, a buzzing fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A large fly that drones noisily around a room is a classic buzzing insect.

clue.text: Crash investigation

explanation.surface: A collision followed by an inquiry into its cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical or nervous collapse is a crash, and a detailed analysis of figures, item by item, is an investigation of them.

clue.text: Fancy roll with no topping

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, so this asks for the opening letter to go

parts.note: the roll of the sea is a surge, a heaving swell

explanation.surface: Someone wants a bread roll but not one with anything on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy roll' reads as a fancy bread roll; 'Fancy' is in fact the noun meaning desire, and 'roll' is the swell of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a fancy for something is having a desire or impulse towards it.

clue.text: Best way, it's said, to produce a vegetable

indicators.note: signals that the words are to be heard spoken rather than read as spelt

parts.note: to best someone is to beat them, and a way is a route

explanation.surface: Advice on the finest method of growing a particular vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAT and ROUTE spoken together sound like the red root vegetable; 'to produce a' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This deep red root is eaten pickled, roasted or in borscht, so it is a vegetable.

clue.text: Birds, about fifty, making for slopes

indicators.note: the bird word goes round the Roman numeral, as about can mean surrounding

parts.note: tits are small songbirds
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A flock of about fifty birds heads for the hillsides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making for' links wordplay to definition; it does not mean travel towards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilts and slopes are both inclines away from the level, as nouns or as verbs.

clue.text: Record, including religion, written on Eastern tablet

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece written on another sits above it, so the record comes first
the record word takes the religion word within it

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A religious record inscribed on a tablet from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The tablet is not a stone slab but a medicinal sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicated sweet sucked for a sore throat is a type of tablet, once made diamond-shaped.

clue.text: Topping builder

parts.note: reads as a first-rate builder, but topping is slang for hanging, so this is one who erects the gallows platform, or more everyday, a worker who puts up poles and planks round buildings

explanation.surface: A tip-top construction worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' is British slang both for excellent and for executing by hanging; the gallows is a scaffold.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who erects the temporary framework round a building is a construction tradesman, and the frame also names the gallows.

clue.text: Obvious time for grievance

parts.note: plain means clear or obvious

explanation.surface: It is high time to air a grievance that is obvious to all.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint, a lament over a wrong, is a grievance voiced.

clue.text: Fellow makes officer grade

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer
a league is a class or grade, as in out of one's league

explanation.surface: A work fellow gets promoted to officer rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow worker in the same office or profession is a co-worker.

clue.text: Vocalised songs prove languorous

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the songs word is heard rather than read

parts.note: lays are songs or ballads

explanation.surface: Sung ballads turn out to be slow and dreamy.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle lazily is to be languorous, lolling about without energy.

clue.text: Lively filly, against the odds

parts.note: F is the racing abbreviation for filly, a young female horse
a venture against the odds is risky, unlikely to succeed

explanation.surface: A spirited young horse wins in spite of the betting.
explanation.walkthrough: In racecards F stands for filly, much as C stands for colt.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful, spirited animal is lively and full of energy.

clue.text: What a jug holds, perhaps

parts.note: jug looks like a pitcher holding milk, but it is slang for prison, so this asks who is held inside one

explanation.surface: A guess at the contents of a pitcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jug' is slang for jail; 'perhaps' marks the answer as one example of what a jail holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone locked in jail is an inmate, the person a jail confines.

clue.text: Tottering, needing set-end hair of the dog after bash

indicators.note: the bash word comes first, with the rest following it

parts.note: to ram is to strike or bash hard

indicators.note: the leading end of the word set is wanted, its opening letter

parts.note: hackles are the hairs on a dog's neck that rise when it is angry

explanation.surface: Unsteady after a heavy night, someone needs the traditional morning drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hair of the dog' looks like a hangover cure but is read literally as a dog's hackle; 'set-end' takes the first letter of 'set' as one of its two ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A building on the verge of collapse is rickety, tottering and badly kept.

clue.text: Choice of work given to lots around Italy

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: the lots word wraps round the abbreviation for Italy

parts.note: tons means lots, a large amount
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Lots of people are offered a selection of works from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' links the work word to what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternative one may pick is a choice.

clue.text: Liberal Government's held by new mentor to be futuristic

indicators.note: the government letter is enclosed by the reworked mentor letters
new signals that the word mentor is to be rearranged into a fresh form

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A forward-looking Liberal government is supported by a fresh adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes ONTERM from MENTOR, and 'held by' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans that look years ahead are forward-looking, concerned with the future.

clue.text: Old circus performer's chuffed, one getting a rise

parts.note: chuffed is British slang for pleased or glad
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tor is a rocky hill, a rise in the land

explanation.surface: An ancient arena fighter is delighted at getting a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The circus here is the Roman arena, not a big top; ''s' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordsman who fought to entertain Roman crowds in the arena was an ancient combatant.

clue.text: To cast off from short pier is practicable

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter of the pier word goes

parts.note: a jetty is a pier or landing stage
on means feasible or possible, as in that is just not on

explanation.surface: Unmooring from a stubby pier is something that can be done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw overboard or discard something is to get rid of it.

clue.text: Party? None in digs is game

parts.note: do is informal for a party

indicators.note: the nothing letter goes inside the digs word

parts.note: mines are diggings, excavations
O, the zero, stands for none

explanation.surface: Asked about a party, the reply is that there is none at the lodgings, so it is a game night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' looks like British slang for lodgings but means excavations.
explanation.definitionFit: A game played with small spotted tiles, matched end to end.

clue.text: Freak NE storm's brewing

indicators.note: a brewing storm is churning, so its letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A freak storm from the north-east is building up.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque, abnormal creature is a freak of nature.

clue.text: Fade away, overcome losing Queen

indicators.note: losing means the queen letters are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: to vanquish is to overcome or defeat

explanation.surface: A monarch is defeated and fades from view.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear from sight is to fade away.

clue.text: One with card reportedly packaging new office item

indicators.note: the one and the card wrap round the new letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: says the card word is heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a trey is a three in cards

explanation.surface: Someone with a card, it is said, wraps a new item for the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the one and the card into a single piece around N.
explanation.definitionFit: The desk basket where incoming papers wait is standard office equipment.

clue.text: Repair tank in US city house, ultimately

indicators.note: the tank goes inside the city plus the final letter of house

parts.note: Reno is a city in Nevada

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of house

parts.note: a vat is a large tank

explanation.surface: Fix a tank in an American city house at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew or restore a building is to repair and refurbish it.

clue.text: Some have no malicious rancour

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people bear no malice or bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite or bitter ill will is figuratively poison, so the word for poison serves.

clue.text: We're told to change course after second set of signals

indicators.note: says the words are heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to tack is to change course under sail, set after tick, a second

explanation.surface: Announcing a change of direction just after a moment's signalling.
explanation.walkthrough: The course change TACK follows TICK, a moment; spoken together they give the bookmakers' hand-signal code, used at British racecourses.
explanation.definitionFit: Racecourse bookmakers pass odds by a code of arm and hand gestures, a system of signals.

clue.text: Fish biting end of angler's line

indicators.note: the fish clamps round the letter as if biting it

parts.note: the cod is a food fish

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of angler

explanation.surface: A fish takes the bait at the end of an angler's line.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord is a length of string or rope, a line.

clue.text: Stupefy with last of drinks — large measure of wine

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of drinks

parts.note: a tun is a large cask, a measure of wine

explanation.surface: Downing a huge cask of wine at the end of the drinks would leave anyone dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze or stupefy is to shock someone senseless.

clue.text: Hard frost outside damaged everything: what's the loss?

indicators.note: the reworked frost letters go round the hard letter
damaged frost is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
all means everything

explanation.surface: A hard frost has ruined every crop, and the farmer counts the cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' turns FROST into SORTF, and 'outside' puts it round H.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount by which something falls short is a deficit, a loss.

clue.text: Music-lover is one likely to enjoy the air

definitions.text: one likely to enjoy the air

explanation.surface: A concert-goer who also likes fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are the BBC's summer concert season in London, whose standing audience are called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a regular at the Proms concerts; the other is someone strolling on a seafront walk for fresh air.
